name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.42.1 — deviations sidecar header is spec-scoped (direct doctrine work, 2026-08-30): the sidecar is per-spec and shared by every worker in a build plus review's own fold, but its header was unspecified, so the first worker to create it improvised one — a layer-titled header (`(tests layer)`) then read to a sibling worker as another run's log and produced a misattributed-provenance return. `/spec:build`'s Worker Contract now prescribes a spec-scoped header only, never a layer or worker name; headers stay inert to the `^- ` ledger count and to the close-time sidecar grammar, so no count, refusal, or fold behavior changes. 7.42.0 — close-gate re-run (specs/20260830/02-close-gate-rerun.md): `/spec:review`'s CLOSE phase writes the canonical doc and folds Gotchas into the host's rules file after the gate leg already ran over the diff, so the files the pipeline itself writes bypassed the host's deterministic rule enforcement (two escapes recorded in salon-os, 2026-08-30). `--mark closed` now re-runs the host's resolved `gateCommand` over the committed close tree as its last refusal check — after the deviations refusals, gotchas ratchet, and dirty-tree check — and refuses the mark (exit 2, `marks.closed` never set) while the gate is red, naming the failed command, a 40-line tail of its output, and the fix-commit-re-run remedy; an unresolvable gate refuses too rather than silently skipping. Gate resolution moved out of review-legs.js into the new shared `spec/scripts/lib/gate-resolve.js` (`resolveGate(specText, config)`), the single `{testDirs}` derivation, so the driver and the review leg can never drift. 7.41.0 — executes-tier collision closure (specs/20260830/01-collision-closure-exec-recall.md): collision-closure.js's paths leg now matches a File Plan target's two-segment path suffix and tiers hits on runnable targets as `executes`, so tests that spawn a script by its root-stripped path are visible at plan lock; the remedy/honesty lines stop asking planners to waive `likely` hits.
